title: pyiceberg-core Python bindings missing third-party license and notice files
summary: Danny Jones reported that pyiceberg-core wheels distribute compiled Rust dependencies without reproducing the dependencies' copyright notices, and said this must be fixed before new pyiceberg-core and iceberg-rust releases, which ship together. He opened an issue proposing a THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES file generated at build time. rdblue confirmed that LICENSE and NOTICE for compiled artifacts must reflect everything distributed and that a NOTICE with the required notices is needed. CTTY pointed to the paimon-rust workflow for generating and verifying per-wheel license reports. kevinjqliu explained that the iceberg-rust source release bundles no dependencies, so only the wheels are affected, and that a repo-wide cargo deny check already blocks incompatible licenses. On October 29 Danny Jones reported the issue fixed: the wheels now ship NOTICE and LICENSE files with all dependencies' notices and licenses appended, the Rust crates keep their original files, and 0.11.0 RC3 is proceeding.

positions.stance: pyiceberg-core wheels ship compiled dependencies without their copyright notices; this must be fixed before the next release, for example with a THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES file added at build time.

LICENSE and NOTICE of compiled artifacts must cover all distributed third-party code; a separate third-party file is acceptable if referenced from LICENSE, but a NOTICE with required notices is mandatory.
Follow the approach used by paimon-rust: derive dependencies from the Python bindings' Cargo.toml, generate a report per wheel, stage it in the artifacts and verify it.
Only the wheels are affected because the source release bundles no dependencies; identify what is bundled and add entries to LICENSE and NOTICE before publishing pyiceberg-core again.

outcome.note: Resolved: pyiceberg-core wheels now ship NOTICE and LICENSE files with all dependencies' notices and licenses appended, while source-only Rust crates keep their original files; Iceberg Rust 0.11.0 RC3 is moving forward.

why_it_matters: Binary artifacts such as pyiceberg-core wheels must carry the licenses and notices of every bundled dependency, which held up the Iceberg Rust 0.11.0 release.
